transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I spend so much time trying to fix how I look before I go out that I end up missing things with my family and at work. It's just gotten to a point where I can't manage it on my own anymore, and I'm really worried about how much it's affecting my life.

What is it that you keep trying to fix before going out—are you mainly worried about a flaw in your appearance, doing certain rituals until they feel right, or being judged by other people? Which of these feels most true for you?

It’s really a mix of both; I get completely obsessed with flaws on my face, like my nose looking crooked, my skin looking saggy, and my jaw drooping. Then I get stuck in these exhausting rituals—staring in the mirror, changing shirts, adjusting the lighting, zooming in on photos, and constantly asking people if I look weird—until I'm so worked up and late that I just can't leave.

When these rituals happen, are they mainly driven by fears that your appearance looks defective or ugly, or do you also have unwanted thoughts and rituals about things not related to your looks? If there are non-appearance thoughts, what are they about?

It is entirely driven by how I look. I get completely consumed by fears that my nose looks crooked, my skin is saggy, or my jaw is drooping. I don't have any of these thoughts or rituals about anything else; it is always about my appearance.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (crooked nose, sagging skin, drooping jaw) along with repetitive appearance-related behaviors such as mirror checking, changing clothes, adjusting lighting, zooming in on photos, and reassurance seeking. These symptoms are explicitly appearance-focused rather than generalized obsessions/compulsions, and they cause significant impairment through lateness and missed family/work activities. This is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder, coded in ICD-10 under hypochondriacal disorder (F45.2).
